related_questions.question: Are you a cancer survivor if you had skin cancer?
related_questions.snippet: According to the American Cancer Society, the term “cancer survivor” is defined as anyone with cancer regardless of what stage of treatment they are going through.

related_questions.question: Is skin cancer a serious cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Skin cancer can be deadly, but the likelihood of this depends on several factors, such as the type of skin cancer, how early it is detected, and the person's overall health. While basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas are not usually life threatening, melanoma is the most dangerous type of skin cancer.
related_questions.title: Skin cancer outlook: Survival rates and more - Medical News Today

text_blocks.snippet: To check for skin cancer, perform monthly self-exams and schedule regular professional skin exams with a dermatologist. Self-exams involve visually inspecting your skin for new or changing moles, spots, or lesions using a full-length mirror and a hand mirror to see all areas. Look for the "ABCDEs" of melanoma: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, Diameter larger than 6mm, and Evolution (changes in size, shape, or color). If you notice any suspicious spots, consult a dermatologist for a professional evaluation and potential biopsy.
snippet_highlighted_words: perform monthly self-exams and schedule regular professional skin exams with a dermatologist

list.title: Frequency:
list.snippet: Perform a thorough self-exam every month.

list.title: Tools:
list.snippet: Use a full-length mirror, a hand mirror, good lighting, and potentially a blow dryer to check your scalp.
Body Front and Back: Examine your entire body, front and back, in the full-length mirror.
Arms and Underarms: Raise your arms to check your sides, underarms, and the tops and palms of your hands.
Legs and Feet: Examine the front and back of your legs, the soles of your feet, and the spaces between your toes.
Scalp and Face: Use a hand mirror to check your scalp (parting your hair) and the back of your neck. Examine your face, ears, and neck.
Back and Buttocks: Check your back and buttocks, possibly with the help of a hand mirror or another person.
Genital Area: Check your genital area.
Moles: Note any new moles, moles that are changing in size, shape, or color, or moles that look different from other moles on your body (the "ugly duckling" sign).
Other Spots or Lesions: Look for any new or changing spots, bumps, or sores that are raised, scaly, crusty, or bleeding.
Changes in Sensation: Note any itching, tenderness, or pain associated with a spot.

list.title: Frequency:
list.snippet: Experts recommend that people at high risk for skin cancer see a dermatologist for a full skin exam at least annually.

list.title: Purpose:
list.snippet: A dermatologist can perform a more detailed examination, including the use of a dermatoscope (a magnifying tool) to better assess suspicious spots.

list.title: Biopsy:
list.snippet: If a spot is concerning, a dermatologist may perform a biopsy (removing a small sample of the spot for examination under a microscope) to determine if it is cancerous.
ABCDEs: Use the ABCDEs of melanoma to help identify potential melanomas:
A: symmetry: One half of the mole doesn't match the other.
B: order: The edges of the mole are irregular, notched, or blurred.
C: olor: The mole has uneven colors, including shades of black, brown, and tan, and sometimes red, white, or blue.
D: iameter: The mole is larger than 6 millimeters (about the size of a pencil eraser), although some melanomas can be smaller.
E: volving: The mole is changing in size, shape, or color.

list.title: When to See a Doctor:
list.snippet: If you notice any new or changing moles, spots, or lesions, or if you have any concerns about your skin, see a dermatologist or other healthcare professional as soon as possible, according to the American Cancer Society.

list.title: Early Detection:
list.snippet: Early detection of skin cancer is crucial for successful treatment, so don't hesitate to seek medical advice if you have any concerns.
